case_number: CIVIL APPEAL NO(S). 10563−10569 OF 2017 & CIVIL APPEAL NO(S). 10570 OF 2017

parties.petitioner: The Government of Tamil Nadu and Anr.
parties.respondent: Tamil Nadu Makkal Nala Paniyalargal and Ors.

summary: The appeals challenged the Madras High Court's judgment affirming earlier directions to reinstate Village Level Workers (Makkal Nala Paniyalargal - MNP) or accommodate them in vacant government posts across Tamil Nadu. The High Court had quashed the state's 2011 order disbanding MNPs and directed absorption or salary payment. The Supreme Court examined whether the State could abolish MNP posts as a policy matter, the applicability of estoppel against the State, and the nature of MNP appointments as honorarium-based roles. It noted that most affected MNPs had joined a new employment scheme introduced in 2022, and 489 did not opt for it despite opportunity. The Court ultimately upheld the principle that creation/abolition of posts lies within executive policy discretion unless mala fide or arbitrary.
legal_provisions_cited: Rule 10(5) of the Tamil Nadu Liquor Retail Vending (in Shops and Bars) Rules, 2003
final_judgment: Appeal disposed of, upholding the State's policy discretion in abolition of posts; no reinstatement mandated as most MNPs had joined a new employment scheme introduced in 2022.
